analyst_view.overall: Shakhtar (21st, 4 points) host Fenerbahce (19th, 5 points) at Stamford Bridge in London, the ground they borrow because of the war, so there is little real home advantage; both need points to stay in play-off contention. Shakhtar, under Arda Turan, are without young striker Kaua Elias, who needs surgery on a broken metatarsal, and the numbers don't list him. Fenerbahce changed coach on 3 November, replacing Ismail Kartal with Emre Belozoglu after a derby loss to Galatasaray, so only a few of the games in the numbers' recent form are his. One match listing has Fenerbahce's Asensio (knee) and Oosterwolde (hamstring) out, which the numbers also don't know; I found it in only one source. No referee is named yet; the numbers already count recent form, including Shakhtar's lively corner and shot counts.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly lower, to about 2.6: Shakhtar lose striker Kaua Elias to foot surgery and Fenerbahce are reported without Asensio, their main creator, and neither absence is in the numbers. The Asensio report comes from one source, so the lean stays small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised about 12% for Shakhtar's busy recent corner count and trimmed for Fenerbahce's. Belozoglu's Fenerbahce are still settling, and a neutral ground in London takes away some of Shakhtar's push, but nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, a high figure that reflects both sides' card records (Fenerbahce about 3 a game). A new coach and a must-win feel for both could keep it tense, but the numbers already carry that style and no referee has been named, so I stay at 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, with Shakhtar's recent shooting run already adding about 15% to their side. I trim it a little, to about 25.7, because both attacks are missing a regular: Kaua Elias for Shakhtar and, per one report, Asensio for Fenerbahce.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Without Kaua Elias, Shakhtar lean more on Alisson and the wide players, who have been wasteful in Europe (they lost 1-0 to Sporting despite good chances), and Fenerbahce lose Asensio's shooting from range if the report holds. I trim it slightly, to about 8.5.
